title: Reconcile invocation tokens with modelUsage, with end-to-end test
summary: Retry of job 145809-7565: make the invocation's measured tokens and the gate's reconciliation rule use one definition (modelUsage), starting from the base because the earlier changes were discarded. This time add a test that runs a result event through parsing, the invocation record and check_invocation, plus a negative case. The audience is the Athena owner, who needs verified jobs to land.

defaults_applied.how: Align the recorded tokens and the gate on one definition rather than loosening the check.
Criteria require tests that run a result event through to check_invocation, not tests that only construct pieces.
cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt --check must be clean.
One focused change on the usage path, with the changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The root cause is that the invocation's tokens come from the result event's top-level usage, while the gate compares them with modelUsage. The two differ when subagents run.

The one definition is the sum of modelUsage over all models, stated in a doc comment on the usage field. If the producer finds the requested model's modelUsage fits the code better, that is acceptable if the doc comment, the invocation tokens and the gate agree.

Older records in records/ that used several models may fail the new check. The producer should keep check_records tolerant of them, for example by comparing against the requested model's entry when the legacy shape applies, or by noting the limit. records/ is absent from the snapshot and is never changed.
The earlier attempt's design was sound; the failure was the missing end-to-end test, so the retry repeats the fix and adds that test.
The final report includes a table mapping each acceptance criterion to the named test or command that shows it is met.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a named end-to-end test feeds a result event through the stream parser and the claude driver (fake script) or the invocation constructor. Its top-level usage differs from modelUsage (main thread plus subagent usage on the requested model, using 90/52656/3634696/134508 against 6/3136/275219/3821). It then runs check_invocation on the resulting record and asserts there is no Reconciliation violation.

Run cargo test: a named negative test builds the record from a result event whose totals really disagree with modelUsage, through the same path. It asserts that check_invocation returns a Reconciliation violation.
One definition of an invocation's measured tokens is stated in a doc comment (on ResultEvent.usage and AgentOutput.usage in lib.rs). The invocation record and the gate's reconcile rule both use it.
The job 2fsa numbers (90/52656/3634696/134508 and 6/3136/275219/3821) appear in a regression test fixture or comment, and CHANGELOG.md records the fix.
Run cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: all pass and are clean, including the existing stream, claude and landing tests.

out_of_scope: Adding a pre-handover criterion-check mechanism to the job runner (already tried for this failure class).
Editing records/ or migrating older records.
Changing governance files such as athena.toml or defaults.toml.
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference, because the change spans several crates and needs the end-to-end test.
